Power the Pacific Northwest: Shape the Future of Clean Energy as our Internal Operations Leader The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is at the heart of the Pacific Northwest's clean energy lifeline, operating one of the nation's largest and most reliable high-voltage transmission grids.

Behind the physical lines and substations that power millions of homes and businesses is a dedicated engine of operational excellence. As the Internal Operations Manager, you will step into a pivotal, high-visibility role as the operational "chief of staff" for our Construction and Maintenance Services division.

You will lead the critical planning, budgeting, and administrative strategies that empower our field crews to execute grid-modernization projects safely, efficiently, and on schedule.

If you are a strategic thinker who thrives at the intersection of team leadership, resource optimization, and high-impact project support, this is your opportunity to drive real-world impact on the future of clean energy.

Key Responsibilities of the Role Here are the eight most impactful and rewarding duties of this position, redesigned to highlight your strategic influence and leadership impact: Serve as a Chief Strategic Advisor Directly partner with senior executive leadership to shape, implement, and evaluate regional grid construction and maintenance programs.

In this trusted advisory role, you will provide critical data, analytical insights, and strategic recommendations that influence high-level decision-making. Lead, Mentor, and Empower a High-Performing Team Provide direct leadership and oversight to a talented team of professional and administrative experts.

You will establish performance standards, foster professional growth, resolve workplace disputes, and champion a collaborative, inclusive culture built on mutual respect and shared success. Drive Multi-Million-Dollar Portfolio and Budget Planning Take ownership of long-range program planning, budgeting, and workload scheduling.

You will oversee resource allocations and monitor third-party contractor portfolios to ensure critical infrastructure projects are executed on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards.

Build and Navigate Key Stakeholder Alliances Represent the agency in critical negotiations and collaborative efforts with executive leaders, federal and state partners, regional public and private utility providers, and manufacturing representatives. You will serve as a key broker in aligning regional interests and securing essential resources.

Champion Process Innovation and Efficiency Identify and eliminate operational bottlenecks. You will foster a forward-thinking, cost-conscious, and results-oriented environment by designing and implementing modern, streamlined workflows that continuously improve operational delivery.

Navigate Regulatory Compliance and Grid Modernization Interpret and apply national energy guidelines and utility performance standards (including NERC and FERC regulations). You will ensure that all planning, construction, and asset-management initiatives align with national compliance frameworks to protect grid reliability.

Shape Long-Term Workforce and Contract Strategies Determine long-range staffing requirements and make high-level decisions on whether to leverage internal personnel or contract work out to private partners. You will design annual and long-range strategic work plans that align administrative resources with field operations.

Champion Safety and Field Readiness Oversee and coordinate critical technical craft and safety training programs across the Pacific Northwest. You will ensure that field personnel are fully equipped, certified, and compliant with safety standards to successfully execute high-risk construction projects.
SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level [GS-12] in the Federal service.

Specialized experience for this position is defined as: 1) Providing program management and analytical advisory services to management in the areas of work planning, scheduling, budgeting, and cost analysis within a utility, construction, production, or maintenance organization; and 2) Performing lead or supervisory duties such as planning and assigning work, establishing performance standards, and resolving administrative or employee grievances.

"Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Time-in-Grade: Current Federal employees must meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement to receive consideration. CTAP/ICTAP candidates: To be considered "well qualified" you must meet all of the requirements as described in this section.

You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

The primary function of the position involves work as a business and operational manager of the franchise restaurant for planning, directing, organizing and business resources to successfully operate and support the installation commander's quality of life programs.

Duties and Responsibilities: Responsible for the economic and efficient management of the franchise restaurant. Ensures all food and beverages meet Air Force (AF) and franchise standards in taste, temperature, freshness, and appearance while adhering to AF and franchise programs and policies.

Effectively supervises managers, staff, and oversees recruitment and training of all personnel. Keep team members current on ongoing/upcoming promotions, business trends, and safety issues. Ensures adherence to all health and safety standards. Estimates food and beverage costs and ensures costs are maintained within established parameters.

Purchases and maintains supplies, equipment, food and beverages at a level that meets current business trends and minimizes waste. Establishes financial goals, prepares budgets, analyzes financial results, maintains solid financial condition, and keeps expenditures within budgetary limits.

Implements higher-level directives, franchise requirements and contract specifications. Formulates procedures and programs to ensure high standards of food and beverage operations consistent with AF and franchise expectations. Strict adherence to policies in customer service.

Manages real property resources and provides expert advice on renovations, improvements, and any required construction in compliance with AF and franchise standards. Investigates and resolves food and beverage quality and service complaints. Implements, monitors, reviews, and evaluates menu items, food production, and food service.

Develops and implements marketing strategies and special events to maintain market share and grow customer base. Establishes and monitors a cleaning and preventative maintenance program for facilities, equipment and vehicles.

Establishes an internal performance management system to ensure proper assignments and reviews evaluation of employee performance. Administers internal control system to preclude or minimize the potential for fraud, waste, and abuse. Arranges for equipment repairs and other services as required.

Complies with EEO concepts and security directives and maintains an appropriate work environment. Communicates ideas, contributions, trends and occurrences to other subordinate supervisors, other franchise locations and HQ AFSVC.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Procurement Operations Coordinator to support the accurate processing, tracking, and reporting of purchase orders across multiple customer projects.

This role serves as a critical link between Project Management, Finance, and external clients ensuring procurement workflows run smoothly, data integrity is maintained, and client expectations are met.

While initially supporting the New York City Department of Education portfolio, this role is designed to scale across Gordian’s growing customer base.

Process, track, and reconcile purchase orders across customer and Gordian systems, ensuring accuracy and alignment to project budgets
Serve as the primary point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders on PO status, updates, discrepancies, and resolution
Maintain complete and audit-ready procurement records and documentation to support compliance and financial reporting
Monitor PO activity across contracts and project portfolios, proactively flagging risks, variances, or delays
Drive continuous improvement by identifying workflow gaps and recommending process enhancements that improve speed, accuracy, and operational efficiency
Support internal teams in achieving customer goals and key performance metrics through timely and accurate procurement execution
Manage competing priorities across multiple projects while maintaining strong client relationships and service delivery standards

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience in Business, Supply Chain Management, or related field
3+ years of experience in Procurement, Purchasing, Contract Administration, or Project/Construction Management
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a customer service orientation
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
Self-motivated with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team

Experience with ERP systems and reporting tools
Proficiency in Power BI and/or Smartsheet
Familiarity with public sector procurement processes
Work Location & Schedule
This is a remote position open to candidates located nationwide
Must be available to work Eastern Time zone business hours
Minimal travel required

Role Summary The Revenue Operations Manager, NAPD is responsible for driving predictable, disciplined revenue execution across a complex distribution sales environment. This role owns pipeline health, forecasting rigor, quota and capacity analytics, and revenue inspection across the NAPD sales lifecycle.

The Revenue Operations Manager partners closely with NAPD Sales Leadership, Finance, Sales Enablement, and Salesforce Product teams to translate Salesforce-enabled selling into consistent execution, trusted forecasts, and decision-ready insights.

This role is expected to proactively surface revenue risks, highlight performance drivers, and improve how the organization plans, inspects, and delivers revenue—not simply report on outcomes. This role offers location flexibility and is open to candidates across the United States.

Candidates based in the Dallas–Fort Worth (DFW) area will be hired in a hybrid capacity. The selected candidate is expected to work on-site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in-office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

Key Responsibilities Pipeline, Funnel & Deal Health Own pipeline health diagnostics and inspection standards across NAPD sales motions, including national accounts and complex manufacturer-aligned opportunities Lead recurring Funnel Health Reviews, identifying risks related to coverage, conversion, velocity, and deal progression Establish and govern funnel hygiene standards to ensure accurate , reliable inspection in Salesforce F orecasting & Revenue Confidence Drive forecasting accuracy through disciplined inspection, trend analysis, and risk identification Provide executive-level pre-reads and insights that clearly articulate forecast confidence, upside, and risk drivers Surface early warning indicators tied to pipeline sufficiency, timing risk, and execution gaps Sales Performance KPIs​ Establish and govern a clear, consistent set of Sales Performance KPIs aligned to Revenue Operations objectives and NAPD revenue outcomes​ Define and  maintain  standard KPI definitions, calculation logic, data sources, and inspection thresholds to ensure consistency and trust across Sales, Finance, and Leadership​

Embed KPI review into regular sales operating rhythms (e.g., weekly funnel reviews, monthly business reviews, quarterly planning) in partnership with Sales Leadership​ Translate KPI trends and outliers into actionable insights, highlighting execution risks, opportunities, and implications for forecast confidence and revenue delivery Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with NAPD Sales Leadership to support data-driven decision making and execution discipline Partner with Business Insights team to define, prioritize, and operationalize Rev Ops dashboards and analytics tools Collaborate with Sales Enablement to identify coaching opportunities and behavior gaps impacting performance Align with Finance to reinforce plan-to-quota alignment and revenue confidence Provide clear business requirements and feedback to Salesforce Product and Business Insights teams to enhance Rev Ops and inspection tooling Operating Model & Continuous Improvement Reinforce a consistent sales operating model across NAPD segments and roles Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve revenue inspection processes Translate complex commercial data into clear, actionable narratives for senior leadership Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience.

Education Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience Critical Skills 7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Analytics, or a related commercial function Strong experience supporting pipeline management, forecasting, and revenue inspection in a complex B2B environment Advanced analytical skills with the ability to synthesize data into actionable insights Preferred Skills Experience in pharmaceutical distribution, healthcare, life sciences, or similarly complex commercial environments

Experience supporting quota setting, capacity modeling, or coverage planning Deep familiarity with Salesforce reporting, dashboards, and inspection workflows Strong executive communication skills with the ability to influence across functions Comfort operating in high-scale, low-margin, high-complexity business models What Sets You Apart You focus on decisions and execution , not just metrics You proactively identify risks and opportunities before they surface in results You are comfortable challenging assumptions with data You thrive in complex, matrixed environments where clarity and discipline matter

A day in the life: The AI Operations Manager is the operating system behind the Innovation team. You administer the company's enterprise AI platforms, keep the SVP and the team's initiatives moving in sync, keep the roadmap current, and act as an early-warning system for what is changing at the AI frontier.

Early on the work is operations-heavy; your strategic voice is expected to grow as you automate the operations down. You are a force multiplier, not a support function.

Responsibilities: - Administer the company's enterprise AI platforms - Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, and new tools as we adopt them - covering provisioning, access, RBAC, usage governance, and billing, and automate that administration down over time. - Keep the SVP of Innovation organized and ahead of schedule through prioritization, prep, and follow-through - you catch what would otherwise slip before it does. - Run the Innovation team's weekly operating rhythm and keep the roadmap current and trusted at all times. - Produce a weekly AI intelligence brief on what is shipping at the frontier and what the team should test. - Bring a point of view into strategy conversations and grow into a genuine strategic voice for the team. - Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department. - Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements: 2-4 years of experience; early-career with an unusually high ceiling and a fast learning rate. AI-native - you use Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini daily and have real intuition for what they can and cannot do. This is the non-negotiable bar. A strong organizer who makes chaos legible and closes loops without being chased.

A clear writer and systems thinker who holds a point of view. Comfortable being the least experienced person in the room and still adding value. Meaningful daily overlap with U.S. Pacific hours (LATAM timezones ideal); remote, open to international candidates. Bonus: you have built something with AI - an agent, a workflow, or a shipped side project.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - Enterprise AI platform access and provisioning requests resolved within one business day, fully documented. - Admin time trending down quarter over quarter as workflows get automated. - Weekly AI intelligence brief shipped on time, every week. - Roadmap accurate and current at any given moment - never a scramble to update it. - Zero missed commitments or dropped follow-ups traceable to coordination gaps.

Most Important Things (MITs) - Be the reason the Innovation team's operations run without friction. - Keep the SVP focused on the highest-leverage work by owning everything beneath it. - Turn AI platform administration into a system that mostly runs itself. - Act as an early-warning system for what is changing in AI - surface it before it is obvious. - Earn a real voice in strategy by being right, useful, and fast.

About the Role: The People Operations Coordinator - Global is responsible for delivering a seamless and high-quality employee experience across the full employee lifecycle.

This role serves as a key operational partner, ensuring timely support for employee inquiries, accurate data management across systems, and smooth coordination of onboarding and offboarding processes.

With a strong focus on detail, organization, and service, the Coordinator helps maintain compliance, operational efficiency, and a welcoming experience for employees. What You’ll Do: Serve as the primary point of contact for all People Operations inquiries via Jira ticketing, email, and other sources ensuring adherence to service level agreements.

Provide tier 1 People Team support such as answering employee questions, people team systems user support, complaint/employee relations intake, verifications of employment, etc.

Properly escalate tier 2 People Team support - such as complex issues requiring interpretation and items needing local expertise - to appropriate People Operations team members or engage cross-functional partners as needed.

Responsible for People Operations onboarding tasks including but not limited to: processing onboards in HCM ensuring data accuracy, auditing new hire data against applicant tracking system, communication with new hires ensuring all onboarding tasks are completed in a timely manner, and scheduling new hire orientation sessions.

Maintain integrity of company HCM and third-party systems – such as local payroll providers and global mobility tools – through accurate and timely data processing.

Create new job requisitions (and positions when applicable) in HCM coordinating with cross-functional partners (People Business Partners, Finance, Talent Acquisition, hiring managers) as needed.

The Bureau of Human Resources proposes a structured, project-based student volunteer initiative within the Records and Information Management branch of the Office of Talent Services (HR/TS/RIM) at the U.S. Department of State.

This initiative directly supports the Presidential Management Agenda and Department priorities related to standardizing systems, eliminating data silos, and reducing wasteful processes.

Student volunteers will contribute to clearly defined, outcome-driven projects, including the documentation of standard procedures, conducting process mapping and proposing innovative modernizations, and updating SharePoint and ServiceNow systems with relevant information.

These efforts address a legitimate agency need to increase efficiencies as well as improve the usability, discoverability, and preservation of operational documents while supporting broader federal data and records management objectives.

The project is designed to align with student learning objectives by providing hands-on experience in process mapping and improvement, writing in Plain Language, lean management practices, and digital records management, while strengthening technical, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

Work will be scoped for completion within a single academic term and will include structured milestones such as onboarding and training, midpoint progress reviews, and final deliverables.

Deliverables may include process documentation, digitized Standard Operating Procedures cataloged in web-based systems, and research summaries that can be operationalized by HR/TS/RIM staff.

Goal: Improve the clarity, consistency, and efficiency of HR/TS/RIM's standard operating procedures (SOPs) by reviewing, revising, and standardizing up to 10 priority SOP documents using Lean management principles, Plain Language best practices, and staff input.

Objectives: 1) By the end of the Spring 2027 semester, review up to 10 existing SOPs; consult with relevant staff and partners to identify process inefficiencies, lessons learned, and opportunities for improvement; research and apply appropriate Lean management principles to develop revised SOP draft. 2) By the end of the Spring 2027 semester, create a culminating presentation to HR/TS/RIM staff and leadership about insights and lessons learned from SOP review, including any recommendations for additional improvements and practice adoptions for the office gleaned from interactions with staff and reviewing source materials.

Deliverables: By the conclusion of the internship, finalize and upload all approved SOPs to the designated digital platform using the organization's standard template, ensuring each document is written in Plain Language, reflects current practices, and is organized for ease of use and future maintenance.

The Compliance Operations Analyst is responsible for supporting Liviniti ’s compliance operations, claim compliance, internal operation audits, and operational oversight functions through audit testing, claims review, data analysis, documentation, reporting, and remediation tracking.

Audit Execution and Claims Review

Support internal audits related to claims accuracy, pass-through pricing validation, accumulator and benefit setup, claims adjudication, and operational compliance.

Review claims data, system outputs, supporting documentation, SOC control evidence, and operational records to identify discrepancies, trends, or potential control gaps.
Assist with the preparation and maintenance of audit work papers, testing results, evidence files, SOC audit documentation, and supporting materials.

Escalate potential findings, exceptions, control gaps, or risks to the Manager of Compliance Operations for review and direction.
Regulatory and Contractual Compliance Testing

Compare operational practices, system configurations, and claims outcomes against documented requirements and approved procedures.
Help identify areas where additional review, documentation, corrective action, or process improvement may be needed.
Maintain awareness of assigned regulatory or contractual requirements that impact claims operations, audit scope, and compliance testing
Delegated Vendor Oversight and FWA Support
Assist with delegated vendor audits, third-party oversight reviews, and service-level agreement validation.
Review delegated vendor documentation, performance data, claims activity, and supporting evidence as part of assigned audit procedures.
Support fraud, waste, and abuse review activities by analyzing utilization patterns, claim trends, provider/pharmacy activity, and other data indicators.
Document potential FWA concerns or unusual trends and escalate findings for further review.
Assist with follow-up requests, evidence collection, and tracking related to vendor or FWA review activities.
Reporting, Remediation, and Corrective Action Tracking
Assist in drafting audit summaries, issue logs, testing results, and finding narratives.
Support the development of audit reports that identify observations, findings, risk levels, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Maintain remediation trackers and follow up with business owners on assigned corrective and preventative action items.

Prepare status updates, dashboards, and summary materials for review by the Manager of Compliance Operations.

Assist with governance workflows related to audit execution, issue tracking, evidence management, and operational compliance monitoring.
Help organize and maintain audit inventories, documentation repositories, trackers, and supporting files.

Participate in process improvement initiatives that strengthen operational controls and compliance oversight.

Review claims and operational data to identify trends, anomalies, potential compliance risks, or areas requiring additional review.
Support automated sampling, exception reporting, and continuous monitoring efforts in partnership with the Manager of Compliance Operations and Technology teams.

Right now, each function applies its own definitions and rules. You'll set one consistent set of rules and make them stick across the entire business. You'll also be responsible for forecasting, headcount planning and supporting the design of commission structures.
This is a hands-on, senior operator role. You'll own the tech stack (HubSpot sits at the centre), and you'll build the workflows, automations and permissions that keep data clean at source. You're not tidying records by hand; you're designing systems. You'll also be working with AI daily – it's not optional here. We use Claude, and you'll need to show evidence of AI already embedded in how you work.
There are no commissions or bonuses in this role and that is deliberate. The role has to stay objective about what the figures say. We've positioned the salary to reflect both your seniority and the independence you'll need to challenge senior leaders professionally and diplomatically when the numbers don't match the narrative.

s.h: HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO BE WORKING ON
s.t:
Building and maintaining complete visibility across the entire revenue line: marketing pipeline, sales pipeline, churn and renewals, and capacity planning.
Setting and enforcing a single set of definitions and rules across marketing, sales and customer success, then making them stick.
Owning HubSpot end-to-end: permissions, day-to-day usage, workflow build, automations and the processes that keep data clean at source.
Producing forecasts, headcount plans and reporting that the leadership team can actually rely on.
Contributing to the design of commission plans and commercial structures.
Supporting the hiring and onboarding of a Sales Operations person, and training them to maintain what you've built.
Presenting to the board, with numbers that are clean, consistent and defensible.
Using AI to solve problems that would otherwise drown you in manual work.
Joining up the revenue line with the wider business (think product, finance, and marketing) so everybody's working from the same playbook.

You've owned reporting across a full commercial funnel (not just the sales pipeline). You can point to a forecast you owned, a commission plan you shaped and workflows you built yourself.
HubSpot is second nature to you. You operate at expert or power-user level and you can configure permissions, automations and processes without breaking into a sweat.
You've worked in multi-product SaaS at a senior level and you understand how different product lines affect pipeline, ARR and churn.
AI is already woven into how you work. You can give concrete examples of which tools you use, what you've built with them, and how they've changed your process significantly.
You can challenge senior leaders diplomatically but firmly, and you're not afraid to report the numbers as they actually are, not as people hope they'll be.
You work best with autonomy. You're a self-starter who gets the work done yourself, not someone who needs to manage others to feel productive.
You'd rather build something new than inherit a legacy system, and you're excited by the chance to define how commercial operations should work.

You've spent your career managing the sales pipeline in isolation, without visibility into marketing and customer success.
You'd struggle with HubSpot or you'd need somebody else to handle the tech stack. This is not negotiable, unfortunately.
You need variable pay to feel motivated. Commission and bonus structures feel essential to you.
AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. You see it as something that reduces your value, not something that multiplies what you can deliver.
You need a large team beneath you from day one. This role starts solo and hands-on, though you'll build a team over time.
You'd rather build strategy than do the work. The first six months are about delivery—designing the systems, building the reports, making it stick—not sitting in planning meetings.

Experience
You've spent time in a revenue operations, commercial operations or similar role, with demonstrable ownership of the full commercial funnel. You've done the work yourself – like configuring HubSpot, building forecasts, and leading alignment conversations across functions. Multi-product SaaS experience is non-negotiable; B2B exposure is strongly preferred.
Tooling
HubSpot sits at the centre, and you're an expert here. Experience with other platforms, such as Salesforce or Pipedrive, is a plus (some skills transfer). You're comfortable across other tech stacks and you use AI regularly as part of your workflow. Other tools in the stack will change and you're flexible on that front.
Communication
You can present to senior audiences without losing clarity. You push back on senior leaders when the numbers don't match the narrative, and you do it diplomatically enough that they listen rather than push back harder. You explain complex commercial logic in plain language.
Research
You think operationally. You diagnose what's broken in a process, you ask tough questions about data quality, and you can identify which problems to tackle first based on commercial impact. You're curious about how the business actually works, not just the metrics.

We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Operations Coordinator to own the job pipeline from intake through invoice — tracking every active job, driving progress at each stage, and making sure nothing sits without action. This role is the operational engine that keeps jobs moving, keeps the team informed, and keeps the insurance process on track.
A significant portion of this role involves direct communication with insurance companies — calling adjusters, following up on claims, tracking appraisal status, and pushing for updates that allow the team to move forward. This is not a passive role. You flag stalled jobs, escalate when needed, and take initiative to get answers without being asked. If you are organized, persistent, and comfortable on the phone with insurance representatives, this role is built for you.
How the Job Pipeline Works
Understanding the full workflow is essential to succeeding in this role:
A new job comes in — you verify it meets the intake requirements and track it in the system
You ping the sales representative to confirm the inspection date has been set
Once the inspection date is confirmed, the job moves to the next stage and a claim number is assigned
You monitor all active jobs — if a job has been sitting without progress for too long, you bring it to the Operations Manager's attention immediately
You contact the insurance company by phone and email to obtain required claim documents, following up weekly until received
Field technicians go out, take photos, and capture data — that data is entered into the platform to generate the inspection report
You use the report to write the estimate and submit it to the insurance company
Once submitted, you follow up with the insurance company on the appraisal status — calling and emailing until you have an update
You communicate appraisal updates clearly to the internal team
Once approved, the information is sent to invoicing and the job moves forward to completion

Job Intake & Pipeline Tracking
Receive and log incoming jobs, verifying they meet the required criteria before moving them into the active pipeline
Track all active jobs through each stage of the process — from intake through inspection, claim submission, appraisal, and invoice
Maintain an accurate, up-to-date job tracker so the team always knows exactly where each job stands
Proactively identify jobs that have stalled or been sitting without progress and escalate them to the Operations Manager before delays become problems
Sales Team Coordination
Ping sales representatives to confirm inspection dates have been scheduled for new incoming jobs
Follow up consistently until confirmation is received — do not wait for the information to come to you
Move jobs through the pipeline stages as milestones are hit and document each transition
Insurance Company Communication — High Volume
This is one of the most critical and time-intensive parts of the role.
Contact insurance companies by phone and email to request and obtain claim documents, adjuster assignments, and claim numbers
Follow up with insurance representatives weekly — or more frequently when deadlines are approaching — until all required documents and approvals are received
Track the status of submitted estimates and appraisals, calling the insurance company to check on progress and push for updates
Communicate clearly and professionally with adjusters — you know how to be persistent without being difficult
Document all insurance communications including contact names, dates, outcomes, and promised follow-up timelines
Inspection Report & Estimate Support
Coordinate with field technicians to ensure photo and data capture from job sites is submitted in a timely manner
Enter field data into the platform to generate the inspection report
Use the completed inspection report to write the estimate and prepare it for submission to the insurance company
Ensure all estimate submissions are complete, accurate, and sent to the correct insurance contact
Appraisal Process Management
Track all submitted estimates through the appraisal process — logging submission dates and expected response windows
Follow up with the insurance company on the status of submitted appraisals — making calls to confirm receipt, ask for timelines, and request updates
Provide clear, timely appraisal status updates to the internal team so everyone knows where each job stands
Once appraisal decisions are received, communicate the outcome and relevant details to the operations and invoicing team so the job can move forward
Invoicing Handoff
Upon appraisal approval, compile and send the required information to the invoicing team
Ensure all documentation needed to close the job is organized, complete, and transmitted without delay

Prior experience in operations coordination, claims coordination, or a similar role in construction, restoration, roofing, or insurance-related services
Comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls to insurance companies, adjusters, and internal team members
Persistent and proactive by nature — you follow up without being asked and escalate before things become urgent
Highly organized with the ability to track multiple active jobs at different stages simultaneously without losing detail
Strong written and verbal communication skills — your phone calls are professional and your documentation is clear
Reliable in a remote environment with a quiet workspace and high-speed internet

Experience working with insurance claims, adjusters, or the property damage restoration process
Familiarity with construction or restoration job management platforms and reporting tools
Background in roofing, storm damage restoration, or property insurance claims coordination
Experience writing estimates or supporting the estimating process in a construction or restoration context
What Makes You a Great Fit
You look at the job tracker every morning and immediately know what needs to move today — without anyone telling you
Insurance companies hear from you on a regular, consistent schedule — not whenever you happen to remember
No job sits in your pipeline without a status, a next action, and a follow-up date
You escalate stalled jobs before the Operations Manager has to ask about them
You are the reason jobs move forward — the team counts on you to keep the pipeline flowing from the first call to the final invoice

## Description ##
## Where passion meets opportunity ##
The best of your adventures is the one you have yet to sail!
## Your Purpose ##
Here at MSC Cruises we are looking for a Public Health Operations Manager to drive and oversee the public health operations in Brazil for MSC Cruises and Explora Journeys, acting as the key strategic partner to Brazil-s National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA) and other government health authorities.
You will champion regulatory excellence by ensuring full compliance with national public health requirements while enabling safe, efficient, and uninterrupted vessel operations.

The Public Health Operations Manager will also lead the design and delivery of impactful seasonal training programs, strengthen high-value relationships across local and federal health networks, and proactively influence public health initiatives that support operational success, exceptional guest experiences, and the continued growth of the business in the Brazilian market.

Public Health Operations & Compliance
* Ensure full compliance with Brazilian public health regulations across all relevant operations, including vessels calling at Brazilian ports.
* Monitor and ensure compliance with sanitation, epidemiological surveillance, potable water safety, food safety, pest control, and waste management standards.
* Coordinate inspections and audits with ANVISA and other Brazilian health authorities.
* Maintain and verify documentation required for vessel entry into Brazilian ports
Policy Monitoring, Development & Strategic Planning
* Stay up to date with changes in ANVISA regulations, policies, and inspection protocols.
* Communicate updates to relevant stakeholders and ensure operational alignment.
* Draft and update public health policies and SOPs for Brazilian operations, incorporating ANVISA requirements aligned with ANVISA-s Guide nº 65/2023 and other relevant legislation, in addition to international best practices (e.g., CDC VSP, SHIPSAN).
* Update outbreak response plans as needed for MSC / Explora Journeys and coordinate with onboard medical teams during public health events.
Liaison & Stakeholder Engagement
* Serve as the primary contact for ANVISA for both cruise brands, facilitating communication, inspections, and reporting.
* Represent Explora Journeys and MSC Cruises in regulatory meetings, industry forums, and collaborative initiatives with Brazilian health authorities.
* Build strong relationships with port health officials, local service providers, and internal stakeholders.
Training & Capacity Building
* Provide training and guidance to shipboard and shoreside teams on Brazilian public health standards.
* Support onboarding and continuous education for Public Health Officers and medical staff operating in Brazilian waters.
* Guide and support vessels in preparing for ANVISA inspections, including documentation, procedural readiness, and crew awareness.
Response Management
* Prepare and deliver timely, accurate responses to ANVISA queries and communications.
* Collaborate closely with the UK Public Health Team and MSC Brazil Legal Team to ensure responses are aligned, well-supported, and strategically delivered.
* Review and challenge ANVISA infraction notices where appropriate, ensuring a coordinated and evidence-based approach.
Internal Audit Programme
* Collaborate with MSCCM Public Health and Food Safety stakeholders to develop and implement an internal audit program aligned with ANVISA standards to proactively identify and address compliance gaps.
## Your Journey so far ##
* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Public Health or a related field.
* Proven track record in regulatory affairs, public health compliance, or maritime health operations.
* Professional experience working within or in close collaboration with ANVISA is strongly preferred.
* Deep understanding of ANVISA regulations and inspection procedures.
* Familiarity with international public health standards (USPH, SHIPSAN, ANVISA, WHO).
* Experience in outbreak investigation and response planning.
* In-depth knowledge of ANVISA regulations and Brazilian health legislation.
* Experience liaising with government agencies and drafting regulatory policy.

We’re building the tools to measure soil carbon at scale. As our People & Operations Manager, you’ll help build a company where people can do good work, grow, and enjoy being part of the team.
**
About Seqana**
Seqana builds digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of soil carbon. We combine satellite imagery, an extensive proprietary library of soil data, and machine learning to make soil carbon measurement accurate, cost-effective, and scalable.
Regenerative agriculture can store carbon in soils while improving soil health, water quality, food security, and biodiversity. Measuring that impact is often costly and complex. Our tools help project developers, agrifood companies, NGOs, and governments credibly quantify and report the results of regenerative agricultural practices.
We’re based in Berlin, backed by venture capital investors, and supported by public funding from ESA and DLR.
Aufgaben
As our People & Operations Manager, you’ll shape how we hire, support, and develop our team, and own the everyday operations that make Seqana a good place to work. You’ll report directly to Stefan, our CEO, and work closely with the leadership team and everyone across the company.
With a new funding round behind us, we’re developing the structures that will support our next stage of growth. You’ll build on what already works and bring more structure where it helps: an HR system that fits our team, a clear framework for development and progression, and a hiring process that brings the right people on board. You’ll have the space to shape the approach and the responsibility to make it work in practice.
Our team brings together soil scientists, engineers, and people in product and commercial roles, often looking at the same problem from four directions. You’ll help keep that team connected, whether we’re at an offsite or working through an ordinary Tuesday. Together with the leadership team, you’ll shape how we give feedback, support each other, and put our values into practice.
**
People**
Own hiring end to end: from shaping job descriptions and sourcing candidates to candidate communication, offers, and contracts.
Own the employee lifecycle, with onboarding that is ready for day one and offboarding that is clear, considerate, and well organised.
Evolve our growth framework and salary bands, and support the annual review and compensation cycle.
Keep a read on how people are doing through check-ins and surveys, and bring forward what leadership needs to hear.
Coordinate our team gatherings, from standups and All-Hands to Thursday hangouts, parties, and the annual offsite.
Build our employer brand so the right people find us.
**
Operations**
Select and introduce an HR system that fits our team, and own migration, rollout, training, and ongoing use.
Own the employee tool stack: licences, accounts, access, and costs per person.
Coordinate payroll with our tax firm and employer of record (EOR) provider, and own the travel expense process.
Coordinate German employment contracts and amendments, visa and immigration cases, and work with our lawyer to move them forward.
Administer our VSOP programme.
Keep our Kreuzberg office welcoming and running smoothly, as a place where our hybrid team wants to meet, work together, and spend time.
Qualifikation
Solid understanding of German employment law, HR practices, and the German administrative system.
Excellent communication skills in German and English.
You’ve built a process, policy, or system from scratch and seen it through to everyday use.
Genuine interest in people and a willingness to give and receive honest feedback.
You’re comfortable moving between a leadership discussion and a hands-on task in the same afternoon.
Experience in hiring, office management, and event planning.
Strong organisational instincts and a habit of following things through.

Experience introducing an HR system such as Personio or HiBob.
Coaching or workshop facilitation experience.
Experience in a startup with 15 to 50 people.

A committed, international team with flat hierarchies, working on a practical contribution to climate action.
The opportunity to shape a growing company in a role where your work is visible to everyone.
Direct collaboration with the CEO and leadership team.

Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen
Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

· ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data

· 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research

· Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle

· An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay sells through two core motions. The first is our new-business engine: a B2B enterprise sales motion winning large retailers and brands with significant parcel volumes — and, in time, extending down-market into Small medium enterprises (SME) as that segment opens up. The second is our field engine, which grows Relay's network of "Pitstops" — local shops and businesses that act as pick-up and drop-off points where consumers can collect parcels and return items.
Both motions depend on the systems and processes this role will build and own: the account universe and TAM, lead scoring and prioritisation, outreach, CRM architecture, governance, and sales tooling.
You'll be both architect and operator, and AI-native in how you work. You'll define what great looks like across the systems and processes underpinning both sales motions, then take ownership of making it happen. You’ll also be highly fluent in metrics — using dashboards and funnel data to identify where performance is breaking down, where opportunities are being lost, and where we can drive greater efficiency.

Build the new-business engine: own TAM, account scoring and weekly prioritisation, plus a top-of-funnel (enrichment, multi-threaded contacts, sequencing, signal-based triggers) that lets sales spend their time pitching, not hunting.
Own the CRM and deal desk: architect Pipedrive around the selling rhythm, govern deal terms, stages and approval gates from pitch to activation, and raise the quality and speed of pitches and proposals.
Scale the Pitstop engine: run the field team's scoring, territories, targets and dashboards, manage pricing levers and CPA, and keep lead-to-live data clean, pushing toward a self-running engine with algorithmic assignment, referrals and AI-handled inbound.
Automate relentlessly: own the tooling stack and build-vs-buy calls (defaulting to building), strip manual work out of the sales day, and design systems that extend to SME and self-serve through configuration, not a rebuild.
Diagnose and fix the funnel: use funnel data to find where deals stall and pipeline leaks, then ship the fixes.
Who Will Thrive in This Role
Systems thinker. You build systems rather than one-off fixes, and you take ideas all the way to a shipped, working solution yourself.
Proven RevOps experience. You've run sales or revenue operations in a fast-moving environment and know what best-in-class looks like across top-of-funnel, CRM, deal desk and process.
CRM owner, not just admin. You've implemented and evolved Pipedrive (or similar) so it fits the selling motion, rather than bending the motion to fit the tool.
Native AI builder. You're fluent with Claude and have shipped real tooling and automations in a live business.
Fast, practical delivery. You implement quickly and are comfortable scoping work for engineering when you need their help.
High bar for quality. You insist on clean data and tight processes
Equally strong in detail and with people. You're comfortable refining a workflow in depth and equally at ease talking pipeline quality with sales.
